title: Learned mitochondrial expression patterns associate with kidney cancer survival
summary: Consensus clustering and Boruta selection separated mitochondrial-expression patterns in TCGA clear-cell renal cancer data, with different recorded overall survival. Iterative LASSO and survival forests also produced exploratory prognostic models fitted to these data. This is a retrospective association; optimized survival cutoffs and model selection make performance optimistic, and predicted drug sensitivity does not establish treatment response or a therapeutic mechanism.
ai_technology: Consensus clustering; Boruta; iterative LASSO; random survival forest

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Outcome associations of unsupervised expression groups and exploratory supervised prognostic fitting using recorded TCGA survival data.
evidence.unknown: Independent prognostic validation, causal mitochondrial mechanisms and clinical treatment utility remain unestablished; no held-out cohort is described for the reported model performance.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised clustering and forest-based feature selection learn mitochondrial-expression patterns that can be compared with recorded survival.
